lesson.child_mission: Rehearsing helps speakers use a clear voice, a steady pace, eye contact and a good timing. Feedback is most useful when it names something that worked and one thing to improve, such as two stars and a wish.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write two stars and a wish for a partner who spoke clearly but read the whole talk from the page.

FEEDBACK
Stars: clear voice and a good explanation of the evidence. Wish: look up more and use short notes instead of reading every word.

WATCH FOR
Giving feedback such as "good" does not help the speaker improve.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Rehearse your presentation twice with a family member or partner and time it. Collect two stars and a wish each time, make one change and write what improved.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Rehearse your presentation twice with a family member or partner and time it. Collect two stars and a wish each time, make one change and write what improved. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Stars: clear voice and a good explanation of the evidence. Wish: look up more and use short notes instead of reading every word. Reasoning: I used rehearsal by attending to voice and explain why it matters rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Giving feedback such as "good" does not help the speaker improve. Correction: Stars: clear voice and a good explanation of the evidence. Wish: look up more and use short notes instead of reading every word. Why: the correction restores accurate use of rehearsal.

Parent: Likely misconception: Giving feedback such as "good" does not help the speaker improve. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating rehearsal on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with rehearsal, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..

teach_steps.explain:
Rehearsing helps speakers use a clear voice, a steady pace, eye contact and a good timing. Feedback is most useful when it names something that worked and one thing to improve, such as two stars and a wish.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a detail is uncertain, identify what source you would need next. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
